## Wiki Manager — Business Requirements & Functional Analysis

**Objective:** Define the business requirements, functional analysis, module responsibilities, and expected behaviors of the Wiki Manager subsystem, so that developers can understand, maintain, and improve it to reliably generate and update a human-comprehensible, living wiki from a project's codebase.

---

### Requirements

#### Business Requirements
- The system must automatically analyze any project's codebase and produce a **human-readable wiki** in Markdown format.
- The wiki must be **self-healing and incremental**: when a source file changes, only the affected wiki page is regenerated.
- The wiki must be **structured into categories** that reflect the real architecture and domains of the project (not just folders).
- The wiki must expose a **landing home page** with a high-level project overview that evolves as the code changes.
- The wiki must be **language-agnostic** (Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, and others must all be supported).
- Users must be able to configure the **output language**, **generation mode** (`mkdocs`), and **custom AI prompt instructions** via `wiki_settings.json`.
- The system must publish the wiki in **MkDocs format** with an auto-generated `mkdocs.yml` navigation.
- The system must also index all wiki pages into **Milvus (vector DB)** so that they are searchable via RAG.
- The wiki must reflect **code dependency relationships** (what a file imports, and what imports it).

#### Functional Requirements
- `create_wiki_tree` — Scan all project files and ask the AI to build or refresh a category tree, then persist it.
- `create_wiki_document` — Generate (or refresh) the Markdown wiki page for a single source file.
- `build_wiki_category` — Bulk-generate wiki pages for all files in a given category (parallel).
- `rebuild_wiki` — Rebuild all categories and finalize the home page and config.
- `build_wiki_home` — Maintain a high-level home page (`home.md`) that updates when any page changes.
- `build_dependency_graph` — Parse all project files and build an import/export dependency graph.
- `build_domains` — Group files into logical code domains using the dependency graph and AI; generate a domain page per cluster.
- `build_wiki_index` — Build and persist a JSON index + index all pages into Milvus.
- `build_module_page` — Generate a detailed module-level page for a single file including its dependency details.
- `_update_mkdocs` — Regenerate `mkdocs.yml` nav section from the current set of wiki files.

---

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `create_wiki_tree` produces a valid `wiki_settings.json` with at most 6 top-level categories, each with a title, description, keywords, and assigned files from the actual project file list.
- [ ] `create_wiki_tree` preserves top-level metadata keys (`language`, `mode`, `prompt`) from any pre-existing `wiki_settings.json`.
- [ ] `create_wiki_tree` serializes any error as `str(ex)`, never as a raw Exception object.
- [ ] `create_wiki_document` writes a valid Markdown file to the correct wiki path for the given source file.
- [ ] `create_wiki_document` appends a `## Dependencies` section when the dependency graph is available and contains relevant data.
- [ ] `create_wiki_document` updates `home.md` after each document is written.
- [ ] `build_wiki_category` processes all files in the category in parallel via `ThreadPoolExecutor` and logs per-file success or failure.
- [ ] `rebuild_wiki` finishes with a final `home.md` update and `mkdocs.yml` refresh.
- [ ] `build_wiki_home` writes a coherent high-level Markdown overview to `home.md` and never exposes implementation details.
- [ ] `build_wiki_home` silently skips when called with empty content.
- [ ] `_get_all_categories` never accumulates state across calls (mutable default argument bug fixed).
- [ ] `_update_mkdocs` correctly handles AI responses that are either a bare YAML list or a dict `{nav: [...]}`.
- [ ] `_get_ai` returns the same cached AI instance for the lifetime of a `WikiManager` instance.
- [ ] `build_domains` writes one Markdown page per domain into `{wiki_path}/domains/`.
- [ ] `build_wiki_index` writes `wiki_index.json` and indexes all pages to Milvus.
- [ ] All errors are logged with `logger.exception` or `logger.error`; no bare `print` or silently swallowed exceptions.
- [ ] Wiki generation works correctly when `project_wiki = True` in project settings; all other operations are no-ops when it is `False`.

---

### Documentation

#### System Architecture

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph WikiManager
        A[create_wiki_tree] -->|persists| B[wiki_settings.json]
        C[create_wiki_document] -->|reads| B
        C -->|writes| D[wiki_path/*.md]
        C -->|updates| E[home.md]
        C -->|triggers| F[_update_mkdocs → mkdocs.yml]
        G[build_wiki_category] -->|parallel calls| C
        H[rebuild_wiki] -->|iterates| G
        H -->|final call| E
        H -->|final call| F
    end

    subgraph Supporting Modules
        K[DependencyGraph] -->|get_file_deps| C
        L[WikiDomains] -->|domain hints| A
        L -->|detect_domains| M[build_domains]
        N[WikiIndex] -->|build + index| O[Milvus / wiki_index.json]
        P[KnowledgeLoader] -->|list_repository_files| A
        Q[ProfileManager] -->|read_profile project| A
        R[EventManager] -->|send_event| G
        S[AI / LLM] -->|_ai_chat| A
        S -->|_ai_chat| C
        S -->|_ai_chat| E
        S -->|_ai_chat| F
    end
```

#### Data Flow: Full Wiki Build

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Dev as Developer / Scheduler
    participant WM as WikiManager
    participant Loader as KnowledgeLoader
    participant Graph as DependencyGraph
    participant Domains as WikiDomains
    participant AI as AI (LLM)
    participant FS as File System

    WM->>Domains: detect_domains(graph)
    Domains->>AI: name & describe each cluster
```
